title: Sleuthboard: threaded request exploration & correlation hub
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design a new 'Sleuthboard' workspace inside Redwood Console for deep request-level investigation. The workspace combines a threaded timeline, span-level lanes, correlation id scaffolding, and contextual panels (logs, headers, KV cache state, cost attribution). Focus is on fast triage flows for production incidents and rollouts comparisons (canary vs baseline). Deliver high-fidelity prototype, interaction spec, handoff tokens for engineers, and a small usability study with platform SREs and two PM customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Users can open a request and see a compact threaded timeline with span lanes grouped by service and host.
2) Correlation IDs should be highlighted and filterable; clicking an ID shows all linked requests in a side panel.
3) Inline span inspection reveals attributes, attached logs (linked), and KV cache hit/miss state.
4) Cost-per-request estimate bar is visible and broken down by model call tokens + infra, with hover to view token counts.
5) Canary comparison mode allows side-by-side timelines for two rollouts with heatmap diff and statistical summary.
6) Prototype loaded in Figma + interaction spec exported; engineers have a single PR checklist for handoff.
7) Usability test with 5 participants completes with median task completion time < 4 minutes for a standard triage task.
design_notes: We want to reduce visual noise vs full waterfall UIs while surfacing signal needed for SLO breaches. Key constraints: maintain 60fps on timeline scrubbing, ensure banding works for very long traces (thousands of spans), and allow pinning of spans to create a canonical path. Consider progressive disclosure for span attributes and align color palette with existing Console tokens. Accessibility: timeline must be keyboard-navigable and have text alternatives for color-only encodings.

mock_review_feedback: Priya Patel (PM): Prefer more contrast for error spans; make error state persistent when pinned.
Marcus Rivera (Eng): Virtualization is a must; recommend using existing span-viewport component from ENG-ui-library.
Nina Okoye (Observability): Add a time-range scrubber that supports jitter visualization for many repeated requests.
Security (Samir Khan): Confirm that trace payloads respect PII redaction rules; add a flag to hide headers by default.
Support (Lena Park): Include a 'share snapshot' link that creates a short-lived artifact for troubleshooting with customers.
decisions: Adopt lane-first timeline with optional waterfall collapse per span to balance density and scan speed.
Implement pinned-canonical-path mechanic (user pins spans to create a focused view of the request path).
Expose cost-per-request as an optional column with token breakdown; toggle off by default for SRE workflows.
Canary comparison mode will operate on sampled traces and an aggregate heatmap overlay to avoid rendering two huge traces side-by-side.
Use existing keyboard navigation patterns from Console to ensure consistency and reduce engineering lift.
Redaction defaults to hide headers and bodies; provide an explicit 'reveal' action gated by role/permission.

notes_for_engineering: See Figma prototype for micro-interactions. Key perf constraint: timeline scrubbing must not block main thread; use requestAnimationFrame and virtualization. Backend should return a lightweight trace summary for overview and provide show-more endpoints for span details. Canary diff endpoint should accept two rollout tags and return aggregated latency distributions and heatmap deltas.
usability_test_plan: 5 participants: 3 platform SREs, 2 PM/customer success. Tasks: 1) Identify root cause of a 95th percentile latency spike; 2) Compare baseline vs canary for a model rollout and summarize differences; 3) Create and share a trace snapshot with support. Measure task completion time, error rate, and SUS score.
